I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so at the start of the season I will stay with the wheat-maize rotation. That is the system I trust most on my land because it fits our climate, our irrigation conditions, and the way I manage labor. I will keep winter wheat on the land through spring and harvest it in early summer, then I will plant summer maize right after. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I care more about stable yield and lodging resistance than saving seed. For wheat, I will manage fertilizer more steadily and irrigate several times because spring moisture is often not enough. For maize, I will push planting quickly after wheat harvest, use more nitrogen than phosphorus and potassium, and keep irrigation moderate unless rainfall is very poor. I will plough before the wheat cycle where needed to deal with compaction, and use rotary tillage after wheat harvest so I can turn around fast for maize. I will not spread myself across too many crops because I would rather run one reliable rotation well than manage several smaller crops poorly.
